title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: GitLab.com
providers.scope_notes: Group IP controls require Premium/Ultimate. Do not transfer Self-Managed 400-day/configuration options to GitLab.com.

controls.name: Restrict access by IP address
controls.what: Limits UI and API access to the group to listed CIDRs, including group/project tokens, deploy keys and CI clone operations.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: IP restrictions apply to project and group access tokens, service accounts, deploy keys, and deploy tokens.

controls.name: CI/CD job token allowlist
controls.what: Only jobs from the project itself and allowlisted groups/projects can use a job token against this project.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions
controls.quote: By default, job token access is restricted to only CI/CD jobs that run in pipelines in your project.

controls.name: Fine-grained permissions for job tokens
controls.what: Limits allowlisted job tokens to a set of REST API endpoints.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions (allowlist entry)
controls.quote: You can use fine-grained permissions to explicitly allow access to a limited set of REST API endpoints.

controls.name: Allow Git push requests to the repository
controls.what: Off by default; when off job tokens cannot push to the repository.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions; projects API
controls.quote: You can configure your project to allow Git push requests that are authenticated with a CI/CD job token. This setting is turned off by default.

controls.name: Limit job token scope for public or internal projects (feature visibility)
controls.what: Setting features to 'Only project members' stops non-allowlisted job tokens reading artifacts, registries, releases or the repo.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > General > Visibility, project features, permissions
controls.quote: You can limit access to these actions to only the projects on the allowlist by setting each feature to be only visible to project members.

no_control.what: Group IP restrictions do not cover runner registration or job requests.
no_control.quote: IP restrictions do not apply to runner registration or when runners request or update CI/CD jobs.

controls_unknown: Whether a GitLab.com group owner can block or allowlist third-party OAuth applications that members authorize (no group-level control found).
Whether a GitLab.com group owner can set a shorter maximum token lifetime than the 365-day default (docs describe this only for administrators/Self-Managed).

authentication.summary: Personal/project/group access tokens, OAuth bearer, CI_JOB_TOKEN and deployment credentials for limited endpoints.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Group IP restriction applies to Git clones by CI/CD jobs, but does not work with GitLab.com hosted runners and does not cover runner job requests. Use self-managed runners with allowlisted IPs. Job-token API coverage is not stated.

renewal.summary: A new job receives its own job token.

administration.summary: Scopes and project/group membership, token rotation/revocation, SAML enforcement and CI job-token allowlists.
administration.conditions: Group IP controls require Premium/Ultimate. Do not transfer Self-Managed 400-day/configuration options to GitLab.com.

sso.details: Docs say Git activity from CI/CD jobs is not SSO-checked.

expiry.ui: Fixed: valid only while the job runs; no setting

reads.ui: Project > Secure > Audit events; filter by user and date, look for repository_download_operation

kill.ui: Project > Build > Pipelines > job > Cancel; limit reach: Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions > CI/CD job token allowlist

token_format.notes: JWT by default from GitLab 19.0 (legacy format until 20.0). Secret detection rule gitlab_ci_build_token; regex not established.

log_sources.name: Job token Authentication log (Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions)
GitLab audit events (group/project/instance)
log_sources.notes: Retained indefinitely. Group/project events need Premium/Ultimate; API date range max 30 days per query. Streaming needs Ultimate.

log_sources.name: api_json.log / production_json.log
log_sources.notes: Self-Managed only. Per-request remote_ip, ua, user_id, username, route/path; correlation_id in production_json.log.

credential_id_fields.notes: User whose access the token carries (pipeline triggerer)

lifecycle_events.notes: Streamed only, not saved to database

anomaly_cues: job token use from an IP that is not a known runner egress
job token used after its job finished (should fail)
secure_ci_job_token_inbound_disabled or allowlist group add shortly before cross-project access
authentication-log entries from projects not in normal dependency graph
jobs from forks/MRs touching other projects' APIs

containment.steps: Cancel the running job; tighten inbound allowlist (remove projects/groups, re-enable inbound scope); restrict fine-grained job token permissions; block the triggering user if their access is abused.
containment.notes: Token is invalid once the job is no longer running. Allowlist changes limit cross-project reach.

sample_query.purpose: Pull 30 days of project events and filter for secure_ci_job_token_* changes
